newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks may salute Britain with higher session.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks may salute Britain with higher session.

text.p: Investors may give Britain a final salute on Friday, the last day of trading under colonial rule, by pushing stock prices higher amid handover euphoria, but a long holiday ahead could tone down the optimism, brokers said.
"There is just a general feeling that people want to end British rule on a strong note," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
With Chinese money expected to rush into the market when it trades for the first time under Chinese rule on Thursday, investors would not want to be left out, Rossiter said.
"Previously a cautious attitude would find investors taking profits whereas now it might be too dangerous to be left out of the market," said Rossiter.
The Hang Seng Index gained 63 points, or 0.42 percent, to close at 15,128.02 on Thursday.
"Technically speaking, Hong Kong stocks are in an uptrend," said Delta Asia Securities senior research analyst Ricky Tam.
"But investors may be tempted to take profits ahead of the long holiday."
Tam predicted a trading range of 15,000 to 15,200 points on Friday.

While the market is closed from Monday to Wednesday to mark Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule on July 1, the U.S. Federal Reserve will meet to deliberate interest rates, which could make investors cautious, he said.
